item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
718
ABPZ20 KNHC 260513
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sun Oct 25 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located a few hundred miles west-southwest of Acapulco,
Mexico, and on Tropical Storm Olana, located several hundred miles
west-southwest of Johnston Atoll.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Olana are issued under
WMO header WTPA33 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCPCP3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Olana are issued under
WMO header WTPA23 KNHC and under AWIPS header HFOTCMCP3.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Mon Oct 26 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 260836
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 AM CST Mon Oct 26 2026
 
...VANCE MOVING SLOWLY NORTHWESTWARD AND LIKELY TO WEAKEN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM CST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.3N 105.1W
ABOUT 260 MI...420 KM SSW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 355 MI...570 KM S OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...995 MB...29.39 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern coast of Mexico should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM CST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was 
located near latitude 15.3 North, longitude 105.1 West.  Vance is 
moving toward the northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h).  A 
west-northwestward motion is expected over the next day or so, 
followed by a turn toward the north around midweek. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Gradual weakening is forecast for the next several days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles (220 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 995 mb (29.39 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4 
inches of rain, with isolated higher totals of 7 inches possible, 
across Sinaloa and the western portions of Nayarit, Jalisco and 
Durango.  Rainfall of 1 to 3 inches is possible across coastal 
areas of Michoacán into Colima.  This rainfall may produce flooding 
and mudslides, especially in areas along steep terrain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance, 
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic 
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect portions of the coast of
southern and southwestern Mexico during the next several days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Mon Oct 26 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 260838
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 AM CST Mon Oct 26 2026

Vance has not changed significantly in organization over the past 
several hours.  There are disorganized bursts of deep convection 
near and east of the estimated center, but convective banding 
features are not well defined.  Upper-level outflow is mainly over 
the northern semicircle of the system.  The advisory intensity is 
held at 55 kt for now, which is in agreement with a subjective 
Dvorak estimate from TAFB and a little higher than most of the 
objective estimates from UW-CIMSS.  

Although the center is difficult to locate, it is estimated to be 
situated near the western side of the main area of convection.  The 
storm appears to still be moving slowly northwestward, with an 
initial motion estimate of around 305/5 kt.  A slow 
west-northwestward track is likely over the next 36 hours or so due 
to a weak mid-level ridge to the north of the system.  In a couple 
of days, a broad mid-level trough near the Baja California peninsula 
should induce a turn toward the north, and the weakening cyclone 
should then move northward and approach mainland Mexico later this 
week.  The official track forecast is shifted somewhat to the west 
of the previous one, but not as far west as much of the model 
guidance.  Additional westward adjustments may be required in 
subsequent advisory packages.

Vance remains in an environment of strong westerly vertical wind 
shear and in a somewhat dry mid-level air mass.  The SHIPS guidance 
indicates that the strong shear should persist for the next few 
days.  Therefore weakening is anticipated as in the previous NHC 
forecast.  Simulated satellite imagery from the ECMWF global model 
output shows Vance losing most of its deep convection after 72 
hours.  Thus, the system is expected to become a post-tropical 
remnant low by late this week.  The official forecast is on the high 
side of the intensity model guidance suite.


Key Messages:
 
1. Although the threat to southwest Mexico is decreasing as the 
forecast track shifts westward away from the coast, interests there 
should continue to monitor Vance's progress.
 
2. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact 
portions of western Mexico during much of this week.  This rainfall 
may produce flooding and mudslides across Sinaloa and along western 
portions of Jalisco, Nayarit and Durango, especially in areas along 
steep terrain.
